products.name: Remote Desktop (RDP) Security Hardening for Windows Endpoints (Intune) — Commercial
products.short_description: Close the RDP settings every assessment flags with one Intune Settings Catalog profile — High/128-bit encryption, always prompt for password, no drive redirection, no saved passwords, Remote Assistance off, NLA required — deployed pilot-first and reversible. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
products.description:
Stop RDP being the door left ajar on every Windows endpoint

Remote Desktop is enabled far more widely than most teams realize, and it ships with defaults that vulnerability assessments flag on nearly every Windows client: weak connection encryption, no forced password prompt, open drive redirection, saved passwords, and Solicited Remote Assistance left on. This solution closes those doors with a single, named Intune Settings Catalog configuration profile that hardens the endpoint as both an RDP host and client — deployed pilot-first and fully reversible.

Run it yourself — simpler, cheaper, and proven

You do not need a consultant. The package hands you the field-tested method as self-guided, click-by-click documentation a competent admin can follow end to end — backed by ready-to-run PowerShell.

  • Simpler — exact, ordered steps with full navigation paths; the profile you create is named RDP Hardening - Pilot and reused through testing and troubleshooting, and every setting is mapped to the registry value you can verify on the device.
  • Cheaper — one fixed price instead of an open meter; a comparable consulting engagement runs well into the thousands per day. Reusable on every rollout.
  • Tested — a pilot-first method (Assess → Configure → Pilot → Validate → Expand) with explicit pass/fail gates, including the one breaking change (High encryption refuses legacy sub-128-bit clients) caught in the pilot, not in production.

Resolves ~5 recurring assessment findings in one profile

  • Client connection encryption level = High (128-bit) — MinEncryptionLevel = 3.
  • Always prompt for password upon connection — fPromptForPassword = 1.
  • Do not allow drive redirection — fDisableCdm = 1.
  • Do not allow passwords to be saved — DisablePasswordSaving = 1.
  • Solicited Remote Assistance = Disabled — fAllowToGetHelp = 0 (Offer Remote Assistance disabled too).

Plus defense-in-depth: require Network Level Authentication (UserAuthentication = 1), a pointer to Restricted Admin / Remote Credential Guard for outbound RDP (cross-referenced to the credential-theft hardening solution), and guidance to limit who can log on via RDP. Complements CIS and DISA STIG baselines as a focused, explainable RDP overlay.

What's inside

  • Solution Overview — why RDP defaults are an assessment finding, each setting mapped to its registry anchor, and the one breaking change (High encryption vs legacy clients).
  • Requirements Guide — prerequisites (Windows enrollment, Settings Catalog, host/client inventory, legacy-client impact, a pilot group) with how to verify/implement each.
  • Implementation Guide — exact steps to build the named RDP Hardening - Pilot Settings Catalog profile, add the five finding settings plus NLA, deploy, verify with a live RDP session, then pilot and expand.
  • 5 PowerShell scripts — readiness discovery, per-device applied-state validation, a coverage report, safe assignment remediation, and a target-group builder.
  • Testing & Troubleshooting Guides (hardened-session tests, the legacy-client breaking-change gate, reversibility) plus Best Practices for one-owner-per-setting and host-vs-client scoping.

The repeatable way

Every solution follows the same repeatable shape, so each deployment feels familiar and low-risk — buy once, reuse the playbook for the next wave and the next project.

The bottom line

Every managed Windows endpoint enforces hardened RDP — strong encryption, forced password prompts, no drive redirection, no saved passwords, and Remote Assistance closed — proven on a pilot before you scale.

What you receive — every file in your download

This package is delivered as downloadable files you keep and reuse across unlimited devices — nothing is left out and nothing else is required:

  • Implementation Guide (PDF) — the complete, click-by-click solution: solution overview, requirements, step-by-step implementation, testing & validation, troubleshooting, best practices.
  • PowerShell Scripts (ZIP) — 5 ready-to-run scripts (read-only discovery/validation/reporting; remediation defaults to a safe preview):
    • RDPHARD-Discovery.ps1 — tenant readiness check for the Windows RDP hardening profile
    • RDPHARD-Remediation.ps1 — safely fix a missing or mis-scoped RDP hardening profile
    • RDPHARD-Report.ps1 — coverage report for Windows devices (RDP hardening applied or not)
    • RDPHARD-Set-ScopeTargeting.ps1 — set the target group for the RDP hardening profile
    • RDPHARD-Validation.ps1 — validate assignment and per-device applied state of the RDP hardening profile

Delivered as a Word document and PDF, plus all PowerShell scripts in a single ZIP — yours to keep and reuse.
